sop_title: VHA Directive 1004.08 – Disclosure of Adverse Events to Patients (excerpt, paragraphs 5–10)
summary: This directive sets out how VHA discloses harmful or potentially harmful adverse events to patients: clinical disclosure by the care team, institutional disclosure by facility leaders, and large-scale disclosure decided through a VA Central Office triage, SME Review Panel, and Clinical Review Board process. It is run by clinicians, facility leadership and Risk Managers, VISN Directors, the Deputy Under Secretary for Health for Operations and Management, the CRB, and the Principal Deputy Under Secretary for Health, who makes large-scale disclosure decisions.

sections.title: Responsibilities
sections.reason: Role-by-role lists of duties that could be reordered without losing meaning; flow-tied duties are drawn from the subsections.

sections.title: Under Secretary for Health
sections.reason: A single compliance duty with no position in the flow.

sections.title: Principal Deputy Under Secretary for Health
sections.reason: A list of duties that could be reordered, but items (1)-(7) and (9) are tied to points in the decision and implementation flows ('If a decision is made to convene the CRB', 'prior to making a final decision').

sections.title: Deputy Under Secretary for Health for Community Care
sections.reason: An ethical-obligation statement and a general coordination duty with no position in the flow.

sections.title: Deputy Under Secretary for Health for Operations and Management
sections.reason: Duties could be listed in any order, but triage, referral, implementation, and After Action Review are tied to positions in the large-scale flows.

sections.title: Chairperson of the Clinical Review Board
sections.reason: Duties could be reordered, but convening the board and providing the recommendation and vote statement are tied to points in the CRB flow.

sections.title: CRB Membership
sections.reason: Membership and voting rules that could be reordered.

sections.title: Clinical Review Board
sections.reason: Mostly a scope and responsibility list, but the review and deliberation duties sit at defined points after the CRB is convened.

sections.title: Subject Matter Expert Review Panel
sections.reason: Fact-finding must come before the written report with one of three findings, so the order of (3)(a) and (b) matters.

sections.title: Assistant Deputy Under Secretary for Health for Patient Care Services
sections.reason: An advisory expertise duty with no position in the flow.

sections.title: Assistant Deputy Under Secretary for Health for Quality, Safety, and Value
sections.reason: A participation list that could be reordered; only the quarterly review in (4) is tied to the flow by its timing.

sections.title: Chief Officer for Specialty Care Services
sections.reason: An advisory expertise duty with no position in the flow.

sections.title: Executive Director, National Center for Ethics in Health Care
sections.reason: Participation and interpretation duties with no fixed position in the flow.

sections.title: Veterans Integrated Service Network Director
sections.reason: Duties could be reordered, but the Issue Brief ('immediately upon receiving communication') and the quarterly report are tied to the flow.

sections.title: VA Medical Facility Director
sections.reason: A responsibility list in which items (5), (6), (7), (8), and (12) are tied to points in the flow by 'immediately', 'if a tort claim has been filed', or 'quarterly'.

sections.title: VA Medical Center Chief of Staff and Associate Director of Patient Care Services
sections.reason: Duties could be reordered; the immediate notification of the Director is tied to discovery of the event.

sections.title: VA Medical Facility Risk Manager
sections.reason: Duties could be reordered; the immediate notification on discovery and the quarterly data collection are tied to the flow.

sections.title: Health Care Providers Responsible for the Patient's Care
sections.reason: General duties that are detailed in the procedure in paragraph 8.

sections.title: Adverse Events That Warrant Disclosure
sections.reason: Criteria for disclosure that could be reordered; they gate the disclosure decisions and supply exceptions (6.d, 6.e(1), 6.e(4)).

sections.title: Communicating Adverse Events
sections.reason: General principles (personal representative, unclear cause, follow-up) that could be reordered; used as exceptions on the disclosure steps.

sections.title: Clinical Disclosure of Adverse Events
sections.reason: Describes how clinical disclosure 'proceeds as follows': decide who discloses, hold the conversation, then document.

sections.title: Who performs clinical disclosure
sections.reason: The harm-level rule that decides who must disclose; it gates a decision.

sections.title: During the clinical disclosure process
sections.reason: The conversation moves from facts to concern to reassurance, so the order matters.

sections.title: Additional support staff
sections.reason: Optional attendance with no position in the flow.

sections.title: Contact information
sections.reason: A required element of the disclosure, mapped as a step in the conversation.

sections.title: Face-to-face, private setting
sections.reason: Setting requirements that apply to the disclosure step.

sections.title: No discussion of compensation
sections.reason: A content restriction with no position in the flow.

sections.title: Timing of clinical disclosure
sections.reason: A 24-hour timing rule and an exemption that gate the clinical disclosure.

sections.title: Documentation of Clinical Disclosures
sections.reason: Documentation conditions that gate the documentation step.

sections.title: Institutional Disclosure of Adverse Events
sections.reason: Planning, inviting the patient, conducting the disclosure, and documenting follow a required order.

sections.title: Definition, requirement, and timing
sections.reason: The trigger criteria and the 72-hour timing rule that gate the process.

sections.title: Conferring with District Chief Counsel
sections.reason: Explicitly happens 'Prior to conducting an institutional disclosure'.

sections.title: Inviting the patient to meet
sections.reason: Happens 'When initiating' the disclosure, before the meeting.

sections.title: Face-to-face requirement
sections.reason: A setting rule plus a documentation exception for remote disclosure.

sections.title: Patient lacking capacity and representative
sections.reason: A recipient rule used as an exception.

sections.title: Attorney request
sections.reason: A conditional rule that gates participant selection before the meeting.

sections.title: Required content of institutional disclosure
sections.reason: A content checklist that could be reordered; each element is mapped as part of the meeting.

sections.title: Adverse Event and Close Call Report file
sections.reason: A record-keeping rule with no position in the flow.

sections.title: Patient questions about investigation; tort claims
sections.reason: Response rules; the tort-claim referral is gated by 'if a tort claim has been filed'.

sections.title: Protected QA documents
sections.reason: Release restrictions with no position in the flow.

sections.title: Documentation of Institutional Disclosures
sections.reason: Documentation rules tied to after the disclosure and to later communications.

sections.title: Large-Scale Disclosure of Adverse Events
sections.reason: Definitions, timing, and gating rules for the large-scale process; the flow itself comes from paragraph 5 duties.

sections.title: Definition of large-scale disclosure
sections.reason: A definition, though it names the patient notification that is mapped in implementation.

sections.title: Issue Brief within 24 hours
sections.reason: A deadline and alternate submitters for the Issue Brief step.

sections.title: Disclosure proceeds as usual when harm is clear
sections.reason: A gating rule used as an exception.

sections.title: Waiting for VA Central Office coordination
sections.reason: A conditional wait rule on institutional disclosure.

sections.title: Decision authority
sections.reason: States who decides and the order of the review bodies; supports the decision flow.

sections.title: What a large-scale disclosure may entail
sections.reason: An optional list ('any or all'); items (2) and (3) are mapped as implementation steps.

processes.name: Make a clinical disclosure
processes.trigger: A harmful or potentially harmful adverse event occurs during the patient's care
processes.outcome: The patient or personal representative has been informed and given contact information, and the disclosure is documented in CPRS when harm is more than minor

processes.name: Escalate a significant adverse event
processes.trigger: A significant adverse event is brought to the attention of the Risk Manager
processes.outcome: The facility Director and District Chief Counsel are informed; for a systems issue, an Issue Brief has reached the Deputy Under Secretary for Health for Operations and Management

processes.name: Make an institutional disclosure
processes.trigger: An adverse event has resulted in, or is reasonably expected to result in, death or serious injury
processes.outcome: The institutional disclosure is made and documented in the CPRS Institutional Disclosure note, with addenda for later communications

processes.name: Decide on large-scale disclosure
processes.trigger: The Deputy Under Secretary for Health for Operations and Management receives an Issue Brief on an event that may require large-scale disclosure
processes.outcome: The Principal Deputy Under Secretary for Health has issued a written decision to close, disclose, or not disclose

processes.name: Implement a large-scale disclosure
processes.trigger: The Principal Deputy Under Secretary for Health decides to conduct a large-scale disclosure
processes.outcome: Field sites and patients are notified, follow-up and any look-back are under way, and the After Action Review report has been submitted to the Under Secretary for Health

processes.name: Report institutional disclosures quarterly
processes.trigger: The end of each quarter, or a request for the report
processes.outcome: The Assistant Deputy Under Secretary for Health for Quality, Safety, and Value has reviewed the VISN reports and sent recommendations to program offices

steps.actor: Clinical team
steps.action: Assess the adverse event's harm and when it was discovered relative to the episode of care
steps.input: Adverse event during the patient's care

steps.actor: Clinical team
steps.action: Determine whether the harm is more than minor, using the test of whether it requires an incident report
steps.output: Harm classified as minor or more than minor
steps.source_quote: If a harm is significant enough to require an incident report or local equivalent, it should be considered more than minor.

steps.actor: Responsible practitioner (or designee)
steps.action: Take responsibility for performing the clinical disclosure
steps.input: Harm classified as more than minor
steps.source_quote: must be performed by the responsible practitioner

steps.actor: Clinical team member (the responsible practitioner when harm is more than minor)
steps.action: Provide preliminary factual information to the patient or personal representative, face-to-face in a private setting when practical
steps.source_quote: Provides preliminary factual information, to the extent it is known

steps.actor: Clinical team member (the responsible practitioner when harm is more than minor)
steps.action: Express concern for the patient's welfare
steps.source_quote: Expresses concern for the patient's welfare.

steps.actor: Clinical team member (the responsible practitioner when harm is more than minor)
steps.action: Reassure the patient or representative, in general terms, that steps are being taken to investigate, remedy injury, and prevent further harm
steps.source_quote: Reassures the patient or personal representative that steps are being taken to investigate the situation

steps.actor: Clinical team member (the responsible practitioner when harm is more than minor)
steps.action: Provide contact information for the designated VA staff who will answer questions
steps.source_quote: must be provided with contact information of the designated VA health care staff

steps.actor: Clinical team
steps.action: Document the clinical disclosure in a CPRS progress note for the encounter, not the institutional disclosure template
steps.source_quote: documentation of a clinical disclosure is required when harm is more than minor

steps.actor: VA medical facility Risk Manager
steps.action: Immediately notify the Associate Director for Patient Care Services, the Chief of Staff, or the facility Director of the significant adverse event
steps.input: Significant adverse event brought to the Risk Manager's attention
steps.source_quote: Immediately notifying the Associate Director for Patient Care Services, Chief of Staff, or VA medical facility Director

steps.actor: Chief of Staff / Associate Director of Patient Care Services
steps.action: Immediately notify the VA medical facility Director of the significant adverse event
steps.input: Notification of a significant adverse event
steps.source_quote: Immediately notifying the VA medical facility Director regarding the discovery of any significant adverse event

steps.actor: VA medical facility Director (or designee)
steps.action: Communicate the adverse event that may require institutional disclosure immediately to District Chief Counsel; escalation ends here and institutional disclosure proceeds separately
steps.input: Single-patient event that may require institutional disclosure
steps.source_quote: adverse events that may require institutional disclosure are communicated immediately to District Chief Counsel

steps.actor: VA medical facility Director (or designee)
steps.action: Submit an Issue Brief to the VISN Director and District Chief Counsel
steps.output: Issue Brief sent to the VISN Director and District Chief Counsel
steps.source_quote: Submitting an Issue Brief to the VISN Director and District Chief Counsel immediately following the discovery

steps.actor: VISN Director (or designee)
steps.action: Submit an Issue Brief to the Deputy Under Secretary for Health for Operations and Management
steps.input: Facility Issue Brief or other reports
steps.output: Issue Brief received at VA Central Office
steps.source_quote: Submitting an Issue Brief to the Deputy Under Secretary for Health for Operations and Management immediately

steps.actor: Facility leadership (facility Director, Chief of Staff, Associate Director for Patient Care Services)
steps.action: Plan what will be communicated, by whom, and how, including the treating clinician's role if a clinical disclosure has already occurred; confer with District Chief Counsel as needed
steps.input: Adverse event resulting in or expected to result in death or serious injury
steps.source_quote: may confer with District Chief Counsel for assistance in deciding what is to be communicated, by whom, and how

steps.actor: Institutional leaders
steps.action: Invite the patient or personal representative to meet
steps.source_quote: institutional leaders invite the patient or personal representative to meet

steps.actor: Institutional leaders
steps.action: Honor the request to bring an attorney and reconsider who attends on behalf of the institution
steps.input: Advance request to bring an attorney
steps.source_quote: must be honored, but may influence the choice of participants on behalf of the institution

steps.actor: Institutional leaders
steps.action: Hold the disclosure meeting, face-to-face in a private setting where possible, and express concern, apologize, and explain the known facts
steps.source_quote: An expression of concern and an apology, including an explanation of the facts

steps.actor: Institutional leaders
steps.action: Outline treatment options, if appropriate
steps.source_quote: An outline of treatment options, if appropriate.

steps.actor: Institutional leaders
steps.action: Arrange a second opinion, additional monitoring, expedited consultations, bereavement support, or other appropriate support
steps.source_quote: Arrangements for a second opinion, additional monitoring, expediting clinical consultations, bereavement support

steps.actor: Institutional leaders
steps.action: Provide contact information for the designated staff who will answer questions
steps.source_quote: Contact information regarding designated staff who are to respond to questions

steps.actor: Institutional leaders
steps.action: Tell the patient or representative they may obtain outside medical or legal advice
steps.source_quote: the option of obtaining outside medical or legal advice

steps.actor: Institutional leaders
steps.action: Offer information on potential compensation and how to apply (VBA and Federal Tort Claims Act for Veterans; Federal Tort Claims Act only for non-Veterans), without assuring compensation
steps.source_quote: Offering information about potential compensation from the Veterans Benefits Administration and under the Federal Tort Claims Act

steps.actor: Risk Manager or other assigned staff member
steps.action: Refer the patient or representative to the VACO National Torts Group for coordination of document requests
steps.output: Referral to the National Torts Group
steps.source_quote: must be referred to VACO National Torts Group for coordination of document requests, if a tort claim has been filed

steps.actor: Authorized CPRS note author (e.g., Risk Manager, Patient Safety Manager, Quality Manager, Chief of Staff)
steps.action: Document the institutional disclosure using the CPRS Institutional Disclosure of Adverse Event note template
steps.source_quote: must be done using the CPRS Institutional Disclosure of Adverse Event Note Template

steps.actor: Risk Manager or organizational leaders
steps.action: Keep the patient or representative apprised of information that emerges from the investigation
steps.source_quote: the Risk Manager or organizational leaders engage the patient or personal representative to keep them apprised

steps.actor: Authorized CPRS note author (e.g., Risk Manager, Patient Safety Manager, Quality Manager, Chief of Staff)
steps.action: Document each later communication about the event as an addendum to the original note
steps.output: Addendum to the Institutional Disclosure note
steps.source_quote: must be documented in an addendum to the original note

steps.actor: Deputy Under Secretary for Health for Operations and Management (coordinated triage process)
steps.action: Run the coordinated triage review with designated offices and SMEs and recommend, based on preliminary information, closing the issue, large-scale disclosure, or referral to the SME Review Panel or CRB
steps.source_quote: Ensuring a coordinated triage process for a review of each potential adverse event that may require large-scale disclosure

steps.actor: Principal Deputy Under Secretary for Health (or designee)
steps.action: Concur or non-concur with the triage recommendation and provide a written record of the decision to the Deputy Under Secretary for Health for Operations and Management
steps.source_quote: Concurring or non-concurring with the recommendation of the Deputy Under Secretary for Health for Operations and Management's coordinated triage process

steps.actor: Deputy Under Secretary for Health for Operations and Management
steps.action: Refer the case to the SME Review Panel for more detailed review
steps.output: Case referred to the SME Review Panel
steps.source_quote: Ensuring that potential cases are referred to the SME Review Panel or CRB for more detailed review

steps.actor: SME Review Panel
steps.action: Conduct fact-finding (site visits if needed, literature reviews, risk assessments) and summarize findings on risk to patients and families
steps.source_quote: Conducting fact-finding, including site visits if needed, literature reviews, risk assessments

steps.actor: SME Review Panel (led by the Deputy Under Secretary for Health for Operations and Management)
steps.action: Submit a written report to the Principal Deputy Under Secretary for Health finding negligible, clinically significant, or indeterminate risk, with the matching recommendation (5.d(3) also assigns this report to the Deputy Under Secretary for Health for Operations and Management)
steps.source_quote: Submitting a written report to the Principal Deputy Under Secretary for Health with one of the following three findings

steps.actor: Principal Deputy Under Secretary for Health (or designee)
steps.action: Concur or non-concur with the SME Review Panel recommendation and provide a written record of the decision to the Deputy Under Secretary for Health for Operations and Management
steps.source_quote: providing a written record of this decision to the Deputy Under Secretary for Health for Operations and Management

steps.actor: Principal Deputy Under Secretary for Health (or designee)
steps.action: Appoint the CRB Chairperson from the Deputy Under Secretary level
steps.source_quote: Appointing the Chairperson of the CRB from the Deputy Under Secretary-level

steps.actor: Principal Deputy Under Secretary for Health (or designee)
steps.action: Communicate the charge to the CRB Chairperson and at the same time notify the Deputy Under Secretary for Health for Operations and Management, OGC, OPIA, and OCLA to begin preparing for a possible disclosure
steps.source_quote: communicating the charge to the CRB Chairperson and simultaneously notifying

steps.actor: CRB Chairperson
steps.action: Convene and chair the CRB
steps.source_quote: Convening and chairing the CRB

steps.actor: Clinical Review Board
steps.action: Review the SME Review Panel's information and risk assessment, seeking clarifications as needed
steps.source_quote: Reviewing the information and risk assessment provided by the SME Review Panel, seeking clarifications as necessary.

steps.actor: Clinical Review Board
steps.action: Weigh the clinical, scientific, epidemiologic, and non-clinical factors and vote on whether to recommend disclosure and whether an epidemiologic investigation is recommended
steps.source_quote: to determine whether a recommendation for disclosure of the adverse event to patients and families is appropriate

steps.actor: CRB Chairperson
steps.action: Provide the Principal Deputy Under Secretary for Health with a plan and timeline for a definitive CRB recommendation
steps.input: CRB conclusion that information is insufficient
steps.source_quote: providing the Principal Deputy Under Secretary for Health with a plan and timeline for a definitive CRB recommendation

steps.actor: CRB Chairperson
steps.action: Provide written recommendations and justifications on behalf of the CRB, addressing patient notification, facility follow-up, and inquiry at other facilities when disclosure is recommended
steps.source_quote: written recommendations and justifications to the Principal Deputy Under Secretary for Health

steps.actor: CRB Chairperson
steps.action: Provide a written statement on whether the recommendation was unanimous and, if not, the assenting and dissenting votes and their rationales
steps.source_quote: whether the CRB recommendation regarding disclosure was unanimous

steps.actor: Principal Deputy Under Secretary for Health (or designee)
steps.action: Request further information or guidance from the CRB
steps.source_quote: Requesting further information or guidance from the CRB, as needed, prior to making a final decision.

steps.actor: Principal Deputy Under Secretary for Health (or designee)
steps.action: Concur or non-concur with the CRB recommendations and communicate the decision to the Deputy Under Secretary for Health for Operations and Management and the CRB Chairperson
steps.source_quote: Concurring or non-concurring with the CRB recommendations, and communicating that decision

steps.actor: Deputy Under Secretary for Health for Operations and Management
steps.action: Notify field sites of the large-scale disclosure, coordinating with OGC, OPIA, OCLA, and other offices
steps.input: Principal Deputy Under Secretary for Health decision to disclose
steps.source_quote: Implementation includes notification of field sites

steps.actor: Deputy Under Secretary for Health for Operations and Management
steps.action: Activate a site visit team
steps.source_quote: activation of a site visit team

steps.actor: Office of the General Counsel and other appropriate offices
steps.action: Review the written materials and statements for the disclosure
steps.source_quote: a review of written materials and statements by OGC, and other appropriate offices

steps.actor: Principal Deputy Under Secretary for Health (or designee)
steps.action: Assign responsibility for leading, organizing, and conducting the look-back program and epidemiologic investigation
steps.input: Need for a look-back or investigation
steps.source_quote: Assigning responsibility for leading, organizing, and conducting any required VHA look-back program and epidemiologic investigation

steps.actor: Principal Deputy Under Secretary for Health (or designee)
steps.action: Ensure facility and VISN leadership are notified that an epidemiologic investigation will take place, and set a clear line of authority, access, and accountability
steps.source_quote: Ensuring that VA medical facility and VISN leadership is notified that an epidemiologic investigation is going to take place

steps.actor: Deputy Under Secretary for Health for Operations and Management
steps.action: Designate and facilitate the look-back activities and epidemiologic investigation
steps.source_quote: Designating and facilitating any required look-back activities and epidemiologic investigations

steps.actor: VA medical facility Director (or designee), coordinated by VHA officials
steps.action: Notify the potentially affected patients or their personal representatives
steps.source_quote: coordinating the notification to multiple patients (or their personal representatives)

steps.actor: Deputy Under Secretary for Health for Operations and Management
steps.action: Coordinate with VA medical facilities to ensure required clinical follow-up is provided to potentially affected patients
steps.source_quote: Coordination with VA medical facilities to ensure that required clinical follow-up is provided for potentially-affected patients.

steps.actor: Principal Deputy Under Secretary for Health (VA Central Office)
steps.action: Notify VBA Central Office that Veterans' benefits may be affected
steps.source_quote: Notification by VA Central Office to the Veterans Benefits Administration (VBA) Central Office component

steps.actor: Deputy Under Secretary for Health for Operations and Management
steps.action: Conduct an After Action Review with SME participation and submit a report to the Under Secretary for Health
steps.source_quote: Conducting an After Action Review of the event with appropriate SME participation and submitting a report to the Under Secretary for Health

steps.actor: VA medical facility Risk Manager
steps.action: Collect, track, and analyze information on the facility's institutional disclosures for the quarterly report
steps.input: Institutional disclosures conducted at the facility
steps.source_quote: Establishing a process for collection, tracking, and analysis of relevant information related to institutional disclosures

steps.actor: VA medical facility Director (or designee)
steps.action: Report the number and types of the facility's institutional disclosures to the VISN Director
steps.source_quote: Providing a report quarterly, and as requested, to the VISN Director

steps.actor: VISN Director (or designee)
steps.action: Report the VISN's institutional disclosures (event date, disclosure date, number of unique patients, any death, departments involved, triggering event) to the Assistant Deputy Under Secretary for Health for Quality, Safety, and Value
steps.source_quote: Providing a report quarterly, and as requested, to the Assistant Deputy Under Secretary for Health for Quality, Safety, and Value

steps.actor: Assistant Deputy Under Secretary for Health for Quality, Safety, and Value (or designee)
steps.action: Complete a quarterly review and analysis of the institutional disclosures reported by each VISN
steps.source_quote: Completing a quarterly review and analysis of institutional disclosures reported by each VISN office

steps.actor: Assistant Deputy Under Secretary for Health for Quality, Safety, and Value (or designee)
steps.action: Send recommendations to the appropriate program offices based on the quarterly analysis
steps.source_quote: providing recommendations to appropriate program offices based on analysis of the quarterly review

decisions.condition: Is the harm minor, discovered after the episode of care, and without implications for the patient's future health?
Is the harm more than minor?

branches.label: No - any clinical team member may disclose

decisions.condition: Is the harm more than minor, so documentation is required?

branches.label: No - no specific CPRS documentation required

decisions.condition: Is the event a systems issue affecting multiple patients that might require large-scale disclosure?

branches.label: No - single-patient event that may require institutional disclosure

decisions.condition: Did the patient or representative ask in advance to bring an attorney?
Is it known that a tort claim has been filed?
Does the Principal Deputy Under Secretary for Health concur with closing the issue as negligible risk?

branches.label: Yes - close the issue, no disclosure
No - large-scale disclosure required (proceed to implementation per 5.d(5))
No - refer to SME Review Panel for detailed review
Principal Deputy Under Secretary for Health non-concurs with the triage recommendation

decisions.condition: Did the Principal Deputy Under Secretary for Health accept a finding of negligible risk?

branches.label: Yes - negligible risk, close the issue
No - clinically significant risk, disclosure required with no CRB
No - indeterminate risk, convene the CRB
Principal Deputy Under Secretary for Health non-concurs with the panel recommendation

decisions.condition: Does the CRB have enough information to make a recommendation?
Does the Principal Deputy Under Secretary for Health need further information or guidance from the CRB before deciding?
Is the final decision to conduct a large-scale disclosure?
Is a look-back or epidemiologic investigation required?
May Veterans' benefits be affected by the disclosure?

exceptions.trigger: The patient is deceased, incapacitated, or otherwise unable to take part in the disclosure
exceptions.handling: Communicate the disclosure to the patient's personal representative; others may be involved as the representative designates under VHA Directive 1605.01.

exceptions.trigger: An adverse event has clearly occurred but its cause is not clear
exceptions.handling: Tell the Veteran or representative what occurred and what is known, whether the problem is being investigated, and whether more information will follow after the review.

exceptions.trigger: An event with large-scale potential is discovered at or near the time it occurs and the potential harm to the individual patient is clear
exceptions.handling: Clinical or institutional disclosure proceeds as usual.

exceptions.trigger: A complication anticipated and discussed during informed consent occurs
exceptions.handling: Discuss it with the patient as part of ongoing clinical care; if the complication is deemed untoward or preventable, disclosure is required.

exceptions.trigger: The Risk Manager notifies the facility Director directly rather than the Chief of Staff or Associate Director for Patient Care Services
exceptions.handling: S10 is not needed; the Director already holds the notification.

exceptions.trigger: The event is identified by a VISN Director or Program Officer rather than a facility
exceptions.handling: The VA medical facility Director, VISN Director, or Program Officer, as appropriate, submits the Issue Brief within 24 hours of discovery.

exceptions.trigger: The event was recognized only after the episode of care and has potential for large-scale disclosure
exceptions.handling: Wait for the VA Central Office coordination process to finish before disclosing to the individual patient, but only if the delay will not harm the patient's health or wellbeing.

exceptions.trigger: The patient cannot understand the situation and has no personal representative
exceptions.handling: Make the institutional disclosure to a family member involved in the patient's care, if available, after consulting the Privacy Office or District Chief Counsel on authorizations and limits.

exceptions.trigger: A face-to-face disclosure is neither possible nor practical
exceptions.handling: Disclose by telephone or letter; the documentation must include the reason it was not done in person.

exceptions.trigger: The patient or representative asks for compensation information that staff do not consider relevant
exceptions.handling: Provide the information anyway, with no assurance that compensation will be granted.

exceptions.trigger: The patient or representative asks whether an investigation will be done and whether they will be told the results
exceptions.handling: Say the matter is being reviewed or investigated; staff may mention FOIA availability and that QA information under 38 U.S.C. 5705 is not releasable.

exceptions.trigger: The Principal Deputy Under Secretary for Health non-concurs with the triage recommendation
The Principal Deputy Under Secretary for Health non-concurs with the SME Review Panel recommendation
The CRB concludes it has insufficient information to make a recommendation
exceptions.handling: The CRB Chairperson gives the Principal Deputy Under Secretary for Health a plan and timeline for a definitive recommendation; the SOP does not state how the CRB returns to deliberation.

exceptions.trigger: After disclosure, the look-back or investigation finds that harm did not occur or the risk is negligible
exceptions.handling: The new risk information must be disclosed to the patient.

exceptions.trigger: Family members or personal contacts of patients who are not Veterans ask about testing
exceptions.handling: Testing of non-Veterans is limited to those otherwise eligible for VA care; the facility advises them of local testing and treatment resources.

timing.requirement: Initiate clinical disclosure as soon as reasonably possible, generally within 24 hours of occurrence.
Notify leadership immediately on learning of a significant adverse event.
Communicate to District Chief Counsel immediately.
Submit the Issue Brief immediately following discovery (5.n(7)) and within 24 hours of discovery (10.b).
Submit the Issue Brief immediately on receiving the facility's communication.

Initiate institutional disclosure as soon as reasonably possible, generally within 72 hours; this does not apply to events recognized after the episode of care, where disclosure may be delayed for a thorough investigation.
For events recognized after the episode of care with large-scale potential, wait until VA Central Office coordination is complete, provided the delay does not harm the patient.
The CRB Chairperson must provide a timeline for a definitive recommendation; no fixed duration is stated.
Collect institutional disclosure data for the quarterly report.
Report quarterly and as requested to the VISN Director.
Report quarterly and as requested to the Assistant Deputy Under Secretary for Health for Quality, Safety, and Value.
Complete the review and analysis quarterly.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: A clinician or unit learns of a significant adverse event, but no one is named to tell the Risk Manager or told how fast. The Risk Manager hears about it late, so every 'immediately' step and the 24-hour Issue Brief clock start late.
risks.cause: 5.p(1) and 5.o(1) begin only when an event is 'brought to the attention of' the Risk Manager or the Chief of Staff and Associate Director. No section in 5–10 names who reports to them or sets a time for that first report.
risks.impact: Escalation is delayed. The 24-hour Issue Brief deadline (10.b) and the 72-hour institutional disclosure target (9.a(2)) can be missed.

quantified_impact.metric: Named reporter or time limit for the first report to the Risk Manager

risks.severity_reason: No reporting path is defined, so delay is likely, and a late start pushes back every downstream deadline for multi-patient events.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: On a multi-patient event, the notice is relayed person to person by calls or emails with no shared record: Risk Manager, then Chief of Staff or Associate Director, then facility Director, then VISN Director, then the Deputy Under Secretary for Health for Operations and Management. If it stalls at any desk, Central Office receives the Issue Brief after 24 hours.
risks.cause: 5.p(1), 5.o(1), 5.n(7) and 5.m(1) each require an 'immediate' relay by a different person. None of them requires a log, an acknowledgment, or a backup.
risks.impact: Central Office triage starts late. Disclosure to potentially affected patients is delayed, and the facility misses the 10.b deadline, which is a compliance finding.

quantified_impact.basis: Map handoffs after S9, S10, S12, S13

risks.severity_reason: Four untracked handoffs under one 24-hour deadline make a stall likely, and a stall delays notification of multiple patients.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: Staff disagree about whether the 24-hour limit covers both the facility-to-VISN leg and the VISN-to-Central Office leg, and about who submits. The brief is sent twice, or it is not sent because each party assumes the other did it.
risks.cause: 5.n(7) has the facility Director send the Issue Brief to the VISN Director and District Chief Counsel 'immediately'. 5.m(1) has the VISN Director send it to the Deputy Under Secretary for Health for Operations and Management 'immediately'. 10.b says the facility Director, VISN Director, or Program Officer, 'as appropriate', must submit an Issue Brief within 24 hours.
risks.impact: The Central Office receives the brief late or receives duplicate briefs, and accountability for the 24-hour requirement is unclear.

quantified_impact.metric: Different timing rules for the same Issue Brief

risks.severity_reason: Confusion is plausible on each multi-patient event, but the 'immediately' wording usually keeps the brief moving.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: A minor-harm disclosure is forgotten or happens days later, and nothing shows it, because no record of the event or the disclosure is required.
risks.cause: 8.g requires disclosure 'as soon as reasonably possible and generally within 24 hours'. 8.a lets any clinical team member disclose minor harm. 8.h(1) does not require documentation unless harm is more than minor.
risks.impact: Patients are informed late or never. The facility cannot show compliance for minor-harm events.

quantified_impact.metric: Target time to initiate clinical disclosure

risks.severity_reason: Missed minor-harm disclosures are likely to go unnoticed, but each one carries limited clinical impact.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: A patient's institutional disclosure is held while the Central Office large-scale process runs. Nobody is on record as having judged that the delay is safe, and the patient's care is affected while they wait.
risks.cause: 9.a(2) sets a target of 'generally within 72 hours' but exempts events recognized after the episode of care. 10.d allows waiting for Central Office coordination 'only if it is determined that the delay will not negatively affect' the patient. Neither section says who makes or records that determination, and the wait has no limit.
risks.impact: The patient is harmed by delayed information or care, and the facility faces compliance exposure under 9.a(1).

quantified_impact.metric: Named owner of the no-harm-from-delay determination

risks.severity_reason: Holds are expected for look-back events, and an undocumented hold can directly affect a seriously harmed patient.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: During an emotional meeting, leaders skip a required element, for example compensation information or notice of the right to outside legal advice, and nobody notices.
risks.cause: 9.g lists seven mandatory elements delivered verbally by 'institutional leaders'. No section requires a checklist or a confirmation that each element was given. 9.d also requires a recorded reason when the disclosure is not made in person.
risks.impact: The patient does not learn about compensation rights (9.g(6), 5.n(10)), creating legal and compliance exposure and a complaint risk.
risks.severity_reason: An omission is moderately likely in a complex conversation, and the impact is legal and patient-rights exposure.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: After the meeting, the leaders who held it assume an authorized note author will write the CPRS Institutional Disclosure note. The note is never entered, or it leaves out why the disclosure was not done in person.
risks.cause: 9.k requires the template. 5.n(9)(c) restricts note entry to specific users, so the people who held the meeting may not be able to write the note. No section requires a check that the note exists.
risks.impact: There is no legal record of the disclosure, later addenda (S26) have nothing to attach to, and the gap becomes an audit finding.

quantified_impact.basis: Map handoff after S22 to the authorized CPRS note author

risks.severity_reason: The handoff to a restricted author is easy to drop, and the missing record matters for audit and tort coordination.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: The investigation produces new findings, but neither the Risk Manager nor the leaders take ownership of telling the patient, so the patient is not kept informed.
risks.cause: 9.g(7) assigns ongoing communication to 'the Risk Manager or organizational leaders' 'as appropriate', with no single owner and no cadence. 7.c and 7.f require follow-up on investigation results.
risks.impact: The patient is uninformed about results that affect their health, trust is damaged, and S26 addenda are missing.
risks.severity_reason: Shared ownership with no cadence makes lapses likely, and the impact falls on individual patients.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: The Principal Deputy Under Secretary for Health disagrees with the triage or SME Review Panel recommendation, and the case stops because nobody knows whether to re-review, refer elsewhere, or decide directly.
risks.cause: 5.b(2) says only 'concurring or non-concurring' and requires a written record. Decisions D7 and D8 have non-concur branches marked UNDEFINED.
risks.impact: The case stalls while patients wait, and individual disclosures held under 10.d are also delayed.

quantified_impact.metric: Decision branches with no next step

risks.severity_reason: Non-concurrence is a designed outcome, and when it happens the stall affects multiple patients.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: The CRB reports it lacks enough information and sends a plan and timeline, but the timeline passes with no one reconvening the board.
risks.cause: 5.e(3) requires a plan and timeline but sets no maximum duration. It does not say who tracks the timeline or how the CRB returns to deliberation.
risks.impact: The decision on disclosure is delayed indefinitely for potentially affected patients.

quantified_impact.metric: Fixed duration for a definitive recommendation

risks.severity_reason: This path is used less often, but when it occurs nothing forces it back on schedule.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: The Deputy Under Secretary for Operations and Management and the SME Review Panel each think the other refers the case and submits the risk report. The Principal Deputy receives two reports, or none.
risks.cause: Referral: 5.d(2) gives it to the Deputy Under Secretary for Operations and Management, while 5.h(1) describes cases 'referred by the Principal Deputy Under Secretary for Health'. Report: 5.h(3)(b) has the SME Review Panel submit the written report, while 5.d(3) has the Deputy Under Secretary for Operations and Management summarize the findings and submit it.
risks.impact: Decision delay, or conflicting reports reaching the decision maker.

quantified_impact.metric: Owners named for the written report

risks.severity_reason: The Deputy Under Secretary leads the panel (5.h(2)), which limits confusion, but duplicate or missing reports remain plausible.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: A case moves among triage, the Principal Deputy, the SME Review Panel, the CRB Chair, and the CRB with no tracker and no deadlines. It sits for weeks at one stage while facilities hold disclosures for affected patients.
risks.cause: 5.b, 5.d, 5.e, 5.g and 5.h set no timeframe for any Central Office stage. 10.d lets facilities wait for this process to finish.
risks.impact: Large-scale disclosure is delayed, individual institutional disclosures are held, and patients face health and trust impact.

quantified_impact.metric: Handoffs from triage to final decision
quantified_impact.basis: Map handoffs after S27, S28, S29, S31, S34, S35, S37, S40, S41, S42

quantified_impact.metric: Possible decision points by the Principal Deputy Under Secretary

risks.severity_reason: Many untracked handoffs with no deadlines make delay likely, and the delay affects many patients.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: After a decision to disclose, field notice, site visit, OGC review, patient letters, clinical follow-up, and the VBA notice are each assumed to be someone else's job. Some patients are not contacted, or are contacted before materials are reviewed.
risks.cause: 10.a says only that 'VHA officials assist with coordinating the notification'. Duties are split across 5.b(6)-(7), 5.b(9), 5.d(5)-(6) and 10.f, with 10.f saying the disclosure 'may entail any or all'. No owner of patient notification and no timeline are named.
risks.impact: Patients miss notification or follow-up, unreviewed statements are released, and benefits are affected without VBA being told.

quantified_impact.basis: Map handoffs after S44, S45 (2), S47, S48, S49, S50, S51

risks.severity_reason: The process is coordinated at senior level, but the many parallel owners make gaps plausible, and the consequences for patients are significant.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: The look-back finds that harm did not occur or the risk is negligible, but nobody is assigned to tell the already-notified patients, who keep worrying about an exposure that did not happen.
risks.cause: 6.d says the new risk information 'must be made to the patient', and 7.c requires follow-up on investigation results. Neither names who does it or when, and no mapped step performs it.
risks.impact: Patients carry unneeded anxiety or undergo unnecessary testing, and the facility is out of compliance with 6.d.

quantified_impact.basis: Exception on S48; no step in the map

risks.severity_reason: This occurs only after look-backs, but when it does it affects every notified patient.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: The same disclosure facts already in CPRS notes are hand-compiled by the Risk Manager, retyped into the facility report, and retyped again into the VISN report. Counts drift and reports arrive late.
risks.cause: 5.p(5), 5.n(12) and 5.m(4) each require a separate quarterly compilation at a different level, with no shared data source.
risks.impact: The Quality, Safety, and Value analysis (5.j(4)) is built on inaccurate or late data.

quantified_impact.basis: Map handoffs after S53, S54, S55

risks.severity_reason: This recurs every quarter, so errors are likely, but the impact is on oversight rather than direct patient care.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: The facility reports only counts and types, so the VISN cannot fill in the event dates, patient counts, deaths, departments, and triggering events it must report, and has to chase each facility.
risks.cause: 5.n(12) requires the facility report to cover 'the number and types' of disclosures. 5.m(4) requires the VISN report to include date of event, date of disclosure, number of unique patients, any death, department(s), and the triggering event.
risks.impact: VISN reports are incomplete or late, and national analysis is weakened.
risks.severity_reason: The mismatch exists every quarter, but the VISN can recover the data with extra effort.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: Decision records, the CRB vote statement, and the panel report are filed in different places by different offices, and the complete case record cannot be assembled for the After Action Review or legal review.
risks.cause: 5.b(8), 5.d(8), 5.e(6), 5.m(3) and 5.n(11) each make a different role responsible for 'a mechanism for maintaining' documents on the same large-scale disclosure.
risks.impact: The record is incomplete for the After Action Review (S52), audit, or litigation.

quantified_impact.metric: Roles separately responsible for document maintenance

risks.severity_reason: Fragmentation is likely, but documents usually exist somewhere, so the impact is retrieval effort rather than loss.

recommendations.label: keep_human
recommendations.proposed_change: The clinical team keeps classifying harm as minor or more than minor, using the incident-report test.
recommendations.reason: This is a clinical judgment that decides who discloses and whether documentation is needed (8.a, 8.h).
implementation_steps: No system change; reinforce the 8.a incident-report test in staff training.

recommendations.label: keep_human
recommendations.proposed_change: The face-to-face clinical disclosure conversation (S4-S7) stays with the clinician.
recommendations.reason: This is a sensitive patient conversation requiring empathy and clinical judgment (8.b, 8.e). Adding mandatory logging for minor events would contradict 8.h(1).
implementation_steps: No system change.

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.proposed_change: The Risk Manager logs the significant adverse event in a Power Apps intake form keyed by case number. A flow notifies the Associate Director for Patient Care Services, the Chief of Staff, and the facility Director at the same time, with discovery and notification timestamps.
recommendations.reason: This replaces untracked phone and email relays with one timestamped record, and it starts the 24-hour Issue Brief clock at discovery.
implementation_steps: Create a SharePoint list 'Adverse Event Escalations' identified by case number, not patient identifier, consistent with 9.h. Columns: discovery date/time, reporter, harm summary, single vs multiple patients, disclosure path, notification timestamps.
Restrict list permissions to the Risk Manager, facility leadership, and their designees.
Build a Power Apps canvas form for the Risk Manager to create the record.
Build a Power Automate flow on item creation that sends a Teams and Outlook notice to all three leaders and writes the sent time back to the item.
Add an adaptive card asking the Director to classify the event as a systems issue or a single-patient event (decision D4).
recommendations.suggested_tool: Power Apps + SharePoint + Power Automate (Teams, Outlook connectors)

impact.basis: Estimate: removes separate calls and emails to up to three leaders. Handoffs remain but become tracked.

recommendations.label: eliminate
recommendations.proposed_change: Remove the Chief of Staff or Associate Director's relay to the facility Director, because A3 notifies the Director at the same moment.
recommendations.reason: Once all three leaders are notified at once, the relay duplicates the notice. 5.p(1) already allows notifying the Director directly, as shown in the map exception on S9.
implementation_steps: Update the local SOP to state that the A3 notification satisfies 5.o(1).
Confirm that the Director is a recipient in the A3 flow.

impact.basis: Removes the S10 step and its handoff to the Director. Minutes are an estimate.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: When the Director classifies the event as one that may require institutional disclosure, a flow immediately sends the case summary to District Chief Counsel and records the time sent and acknowledged.
recommendations.reason: 5.n(6) requires 'immediately'. The trigger is rule-based once the classification is made.
implementation_steps: Add a 'District Chief Counsel notified' timestamp column to the A3 list.
Create a flow triggered when the disclosure path is set to institutional.
Send an Outlook email and Teams message to the District Chief Counsel mailbox containing the case number and summary only.
Request an acknowledgment with an adaptive card and log the response time on the item.

impact.occurrence: per event that may require institutional disclosure
impact.basis: Removes retyping the event details into a separate email to counsel. Minutes are an estimate.

recommendations.label: ai_assist
recommendations.proposed_change: For a systems-issue event, an AI step drafts the Issue Brief from the intake record. The Director edits and approves it, and the flow sends it to the VISN Director and District Chief Counsel, with reminders before the 24-hour mark.
recommendations.reason: Drafting from facts already captured removes retyping, and the clock enforces 10.b.
implementation_steps: Create a Word Issue Brief template in a restricted SharePoint library.
In the flow, use an AI Builder prompt (or Copilot) to draft brief sections from the A3 item fields.
Populate the template with 'Populate a Microsoft Word template' and save it to the case folder.
Route the draft to the Director with Approvals; on approval, email it to the VISN Director and District Chief Counsel.
Add a delay-until check that alerts the Director and VISN at 18 hours if the brief has not been sent. The 18-hour threshold is configurable, not from the SOP.
recommendations.suggested_tool: Power Automate + AI Builder + Word Online (Business) + Approvals

impact.basis: Removes re-entry of intake facts into the brief. Minutes are an estimate.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: The VISN Director reviews the facility Issue Brief in an approval. On approval, the flow forwards it to the Deputy Under Secretary for Health for Operations and Management and creates the Central Office case record.
recommendations.reason: This removes a second manual send, gives the Central Office a tracked intake, and shows clearly who submitted and when (10.b).
implementation_steps: Add an approval step for the VISN Director to the A6 flow.
On approval, email the brief to the Deputy Under Secretary for Health for Operations and Management mailbox.
Create an item in a Central Office 'Large-Scale Disclosure Cases' list, linked by case number.
Log submitter and timestamps so the policy owner can confirm the 24-hour reading of 10.b against 5.n(7) and 5.m(1).

impact.basis: Removes re-sending or retyping the brief. Minutes are an estimate.

recommendations.label: keep_human
recommendations.proposed_change: Facility leadership keeps planning what is said, by whom, and how, conferring with District Chief Counsel.
recommendations.reason: This involves legal and ethical judgment (9.b).
implementation_steps: No system change.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: When an event is flagged for institutional disclosure, a flow sets the 72-hour target, or records a 10.d hold with the name of the person who determined the delay is safe, and reminds leaders until the invitation date is logged.
recommendations.reason: This makes the 72-hour target and the 10.d hold decision visible and owned.
implementation_steps: Add columns to the A3 list: recognized after the episode of care (Y/N), 10.d hold (Y/N), hold determined by, hold rationale, invitation date.
Create a flow that calculates the target as discovery plus 72 hours when not exempt.
Send reminders at intervals to the leaders until the invitation date is filled. Intervals are configurable.
When the 10.d hold is set, require 'hold determined by' and rationale before saving, and send a weekly status reminder while the Central Office case is open.

recommendations.label: keep_human
recommendations.proposed_change: Leaders keep deciding who attends when the patient brings an attorney.
recommendations.reason: This is a legal and participant-selection judgment (9.f).
implementation_steps: No system change.

recommendations.label: keep_human
recommendations.proposed_change: The disclosure meeting, apology, and explanation of facts stay with institutional leaders, in person where possible.
recommendations.reason: This is a sensitive conversation with legal weight (9.d, 9.g(1)).
implementation_steps: No system change.

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.proposed_change: Leaders complete a Power Apps disclosure checklist confirming each 9.g element. The app shows the right compensation information for the patient's Veteran status. The checklist also records modality, the reason if not in person, and the 5.m(4) reporting fields.
recommendations.reason: This gives a confirmation control over the required content and captures the quarterly reporting data once, at the source.
implementation_steps: Create a SharePoint list 'Institutional Disclosure Checklist' linked by case number.

Add fields: each 9.g element (Y/N), Veteran status, modality, reason not in person, tort claim known (Y/N), date of event, date of disclosure, number of unique patients, death (Y/N), departments, triggering event.
Build a Power Apps form that shows VBA plus Federal Tort Claims Act guidance for Veterans and Federal Tort Claims Act guidance only for non-Veterans.
Make the 9.g fields required before submission.

impact.basis: Estimate: replaces ad-hoc notes. Feeds A14 and A34.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: If the checklist shows a known tort claim, a flow assigns the Risk Manager a task to refer the patient to the VACO National Torts Group and tracks completion.
recommendations.reason: This is a rule-based trigger (9.i, 5.n(5)).
implementation_steps: Trigger on a checklist item where 'tort claim known' is Yes.
Create a Planner task for the Risk Manager containing the National Torts Group referral contact template.
Write the completion date back to the checklist.

impact.occurrence: per institutional disclosure with a known tort claim

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: When the checklist is submitted, a flow assigns the authorized CPRS note author a task to enter the Institutional Disclosure note, including the remote-modality reason if applicable, and reminds them until it is confirmed.
recommendations.reason: This closes the untracked handoff to a restricted note author (5.n(9)(c), 9.k).
implementation_steps: Trigger on creation of a checklist item.
Create a Planner task, or send a Teams adaptive card, to the designated note author with the case number and modality and reason.
Send recurring reminders until the author marks 'CPRS note entered'.
Record the confirmation time on the checklist item.

impact.basis: Estimate. CPRS entry itself remains manual; there is no M365 connector to CPRS.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: The checklist names a single owner for ongoing communication. A flow reminds that owner on a set cadence while the investigation is open, and prompts a CPRS addendum (S26) after each contact.
recommendations.reason: This turns 'Risk Manager or organizational leaders as appropriate' into a named, scheduled duty (9.g(7)).
implementation_steps: Add 'communication owner' (person) and 'investigation open' fields to the checklist.
Create a scheduled flow that reminds the owner at a configurable cadence.
When the owner logs a contact, create a reminder to the note author to add the S26 addendum.

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.proposed_change: The coordinated triage records its recommendation (close, disclose, refer to the SME Review Panel, or convene the CRB) in the Central Office case tracker. The tracker shows the stage, owner, and age of every case and holds all case documents in one library.
recommendations.reason: This gives one case record and status view across all stages, and one document location for 5.b(8), 5.d(8), and 5.e(6).
implementation_steps: Extend the A7 'Large-Scale Disclosure Cases' list with stage, current owner, stage start date, recommendation, and named referrer and report submitter.
Create a document library with a folder per case, restricted to Central Office participants.
Build a Power Apps screen for triage staff to record the recommendation.
Add a list view or Power BI page showing days in stage for each case.
Ask the policy owner to set one owner for referral and for the report (5.d(2) vs 5.h(1); 5.d(3) vs 5.h(3)(b)) and record that owner in the tracker.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: The triage recommendation goes to the Principal Deputy Under Secretary for Health as an approval. Concur or non-concur is stored as the written record and sent to the Deputy Under Secretary for Operations and Management. A non-concur requires the decision maker to choose the next path.
recommendations.reason: This produces the written record automatically (5.b(2)) and closes the UNDEFINED non-concur branch of D7. The decision itself stays human.
implementation_steps: Trigger when the triage recommendation is saved in the case tracker.
Start an Approvals action ('Approve with options': concur, non-concur) assigned to the Principal Deputy or designee.
On non-concur, require a selected next path: refer to SME Review Panel, convene CRB, disclose, or close. Ask the policy owner to confirm these options.
Save the response and comments as a PDF decision record in the case library and email it to the Deputy Under Secretary for Operations and Management.
Update the case stage and owner.

impact.basis: Removes writing a separate decision memo. Minutes are an estimate.

recommendations.label: ai_assist
recommendations.proposed_change: An AI step summarizes uploaded site-visit notes and literature into a draft findings summary on probability and severity of harm. The SME Review Panel verifies it and makes all risk judgments.
recommendations.reason: This reduces reading and summarizing time. The risk assessment remains panel judgment (5.h(3)(a)).
implementation_steps: Have the panel upload fact-finding documents to the case library.
Run an AI Builder or Copilot prompt that drafts a summary structured by probability of harm and severity of harm.
Save the draft to the case folder marked 'AI draft – requires panel review'.
recommendations.suggested_tool: Power Automate + AI Builder (or Microsoft 365 Copilot)

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.proposed_change: The SME Review Panel's written report becomes a structured form. It requires exactly one of the three findings with its matching recommendation, and a named submitter, and it routes to the Principal Deputy Under Secretary for Health.
recommendations.reason: This enforces the three-finding format (5.h(3)(b)) and records a single submitter, which addresses the 5.d(3) vs 5.h(3)(b) overlap once the policy owner sets the owner.
implementation_steps: Add report fields to the case tracker: finding (negligible, clinically significant, or indeterminate), rationale, submitter.
Build a Power Apps form with finding as a required single choice.
Generate a PDF report into the case library on submission.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: The A17 approval pattern is reused for the SME Review Panel report: concur or non-concur, a required next path on non-concur, and an automatic written record.
recommendations.reason: This closes the UNDEFINED non-concur branch of D8 and produces the 5.b(2) record.
implementation_steps: Trigger the A17 approval child flow when the A19 report is submitted.
Map options to D8 outcomes: close, disclose (go to implementation), or convene the CRB.
Store the decision record and update the stage.

impact.basis: Removes a separate decision memo. Minutes are an estimate.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: When the decision is to convene the CRB, one flow sends the charge to the CRB Chairperson and the preparation notices to the Deputy Under Secretary for Operations and Management, OGC, OPIA, and OCLA at the same time.
recommendations.reason: 5.b(3) requires these notices 'simultaneously'. The recipients are fixed.
implementation_steps: Trigger when the case stage changes to 'Convene CRB'.
Send the charge, with links to the case documents, to the Chair.
Send the parallel notices to the office mailboxes.
Log the send times on the case.

impact.basis: Five recipients receive one generated message instead of separately written ones (4 fewer). Minutes are an estimate.

recommendations.label: keep_human
recommendations.proposed_change: CRB deliberation and voting on disclosure and on any epidemiologic investigation stay with the board.
recommendations.reason: This is an ethical and clinical judgment about patients (5.g(3)).
implementation_steps: No system change.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: The CRB Chair records the plan and the target date for a definitive recommendation in the tracker. The flow reminds the Chair before that date and alerts the Principal Deputy if it passes without a recommendation.
recommendations.reason: This gives the 5.e(3) timeline a tracked return path.
implementation_steps: Add 'plan' and 'definitive recommendation due' fields to the case.
Create a scheduled flow that checks the due date daily.
Send reminders to the Chair before the date and an overdue alert to the Principal Deputy after it.

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.proposed_change: The CRB Chair submits one structured recommendation form. It includes the recommendation, the justification, the required 5.e(5) elements when disclosure is recommended, and the vote tally with assenting and dissenting rationales.
recommendations.reason: This makes sure the 5.e(4) and 5.e(5) content is complete and puts it in one submission.
implementation_steps: Add fields: recommendation, justification, patient notification plan, facility follow-up, inquiry at other facilities, unanimous (Y/N), assent count, dissent count, rationales.
Build a Power Apps form; make the 5.e(5) fields required when the recommendation is to disclose.
Generate a PDF into the case library and notify the Principal Deputy.

recommendations.label: eliminate
recommendations.proposed_change: The separate vote statement is folded into the A24 recommendation form as a required section.
recommendations.reason: The vote statement goes from the same author to the same recipient at the same time. 5.e(4) is still met as a section of the submission.
implementation_steps: Include the vote fields in the A24 form.
Note in the local SOP that the A24 submission satisfies 5.e(4).

impact.basis: Removes step S40 and its separate document. The handoff to the Principal Deputy remains via the A24 submission. Minutes are an estimate.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: The Principal Deputy concurs or non-concurs with the CRB recommendation in an approval, with an option to request more information (S41). The decision is stored and sent automatically to the Deputy Under Secretary for Operations and Management and the CRB Chair.
recommendations.reason: This removes manual decision memos and gives the case its final tracked status (5.b(4)).
implementation_steps: Trigger when the A24 form is submitted.
Start an Approvals action with options: concur, non-concur, request more information.
On 'request more information', notify the Chair and reset the stage.
Otherwise, store the PDF decision record and email it to both recipients.
On a decision to disclose, set the stage to Implementation, which triggers A27.

impact.basis: Removes a separately written decision communication. Minutes are an estimate.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: A decision to disclose triggers a flow that notifies field sites and OGC, OPIA, and OCLA. It also creates an implementation tracker with a named owner and task for each activity: site visit, OGC review, look-back, patient notification, clinical follow-up, and VBA notice.
recommendations.reason: This gives clear ownership of the parallel implementation activities in 5.d(5) and 10.f.
implementation_steps: Create a Planner plan per case from a template, with tasks for S44, S45, S46-S48, S49, S50, and S51.
Have the flow send notices to field-site leadership and the program office mailboxes.
Require an owner for each task, including a named owner for patient notification (10.a).
Add a gate so the patient-notification task cannot be marked ready until the OGC review task is complete.

recommendations.label: keep_human
recommendations.proposed_change: OGC and other offices keep reviewing all written materials and statements.
recommendations.reason: This is a legal sign-off (5.d(5)).
implementation_steps: No system change; tracked as a task in A27.

recommendations.label: keep_human
recommendations.proposed_change: The Principal Deputy keeps assigning the look-back and epidemiologic investigation lead.
recommendations.reason: This is a leadership decision about people and accountability (5.b(9)).
implementation_steps: No system change; record the assignee in the A27 tracker.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: Look-back results are recorded in the case tracker. When the result is 'harm did not occur' or 'negligible risk', a flow creates a re-disclosure task for the patient-notification owner, so notified patients get the new information required by 6.d.
recommendations.reason: This gives the 6.d and 7.c follow-up an owner and a trigger.
implementation_steps: Add 'look-back result' and 'result date' fields to the case.
Trigger on a result of 'no harm' or 'negligible'.
Create a Planner task for the named patient-notification owner and set the case to 'Re-disclosure pending'.

recommendations.label: keep_human
recommendations.proposed_change: Notifying potentially affected patients and representatives stays with designated facility staff.
recommendations.reason: This is sensitive communication subject to privacy limits (10.e, 7.d, 7.e).
implementation_steps: No system change; track completion in the A27 plan.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: When the case is flagged 'Veterans' benefits may be affected', a flow sends the prepared notice to VBA Central Office and logs it.
recommendations.reason: This is a rule-based notification (5.b(6), 10.f(3)).
implementation_steps: Add a 'benefits may be affected' flag to the case.
Trigger the flow on the flag.
Send an Outlook email to the VBA Central Office contact with Principal Deputy office approval, and log the send time.

recommendations.label: ai_assist
recommendations.proposed_change: An AI step drafts the After Action Review timeline and summary from the case tracker history and documents. The Deputy Under Secretary for Operations and Management and the SMEs revise it and submit it to the Under Secretary for Health.
recommendations.reason: The tracker holds the full timeline, so drafting from it saves compilation time. Findings remain human.
implementation_steps: Export case stage history and timestamps from the tracker.
Run an AI Builder or Copilot prompt to draft the chronology and stage durations.
Save the draft to the case library for SME review and submission.
recommendations.suggested_tool: Power Automate + AI Builder (or Microsoft 365 Copilot in Word)

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: A scheduled flow compiles the facility's quarterly institutional disclosure data, including all 5.m(4) fields, from the A12 checklist list instead of the Risk Manager compiling it by hand.
recommendations.reason: This removes re-collection of data already captured at disclosure and fixes the facility/VISN field mismatch.
implementation_steps: Create a scheduled flow that runs at quarter end, or on request.
Filter checklist items by disclosure date in the quarter.
Generate an Excel or Word quarterly report with counts by type and the 5.m(4) fields.
Send it to the Risk Manager for verification.

impact.basis: Removes one manual compilation. Minutes are an estimate.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: The facility Director approves the generated quarterly report in Approvals, and the flow submits it to the VISN Director.
recommendations.reason: This removes retyping and keeps the 5.n(12) Director accountability.
implementation_steps: Chain an Approvals action to A34, assigned to the Director.
On approval, email the report to the VISN Director and save it to the VISN library.

impact.basis: Removes one re-entry. Minutes are an estimate.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: A flow rolls up the approved facility reports into the VISN report with the 5.m(4) fields. The VISN Director approves it and it is submitted to Quality, Safety, and Value.
recommendations.reason: This removes the third manual compilation.
implementation_steps: Trigger when all facility reports for the quarter are in the VISN library, or at a set date.
Merge the facility data into the VISN report template.
Route to the VISN Director for approval, then send to the Assistant Deputy Under Secretary for Quality, Safety, and Value.

impact.basis: Removes one re-entry. Minutes are an estimate.

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.proposed_change: The Assistant Deputy Under Secretary for Quality, Safety, and Value reviews a Power BI dashboard built on the VISN report data instead of compiling the reports by hand.
recommendations.reason: This speeds the quarterly analysis (5.j(4)).
implementation_steps: Connect Power BI to the VISN report library.
Build visuals by VISN, department, triggering event, deaths, and event-to-disclosure interval.
Refresh on report submission.

recommendations.label: keep_human
recommendations.proposed_change: Recommendations to program offices stay with the Quality, Safety, and Value office.
recommendations.reason: This is an analytical and policy judgment.
implementation_steps: No system change.

starter_flows.trigger: SharePoint – When an item is created or modified in 'Adverse Event Escalations', with trigger condition: Disclosure path = 'Institutional disclosure may be required' AND 'District Chief Counsel notified' is empty
actions: Get item (case number, discovery date/time, harm summary; no patient identifiers)
Compose message body from the case fields
Send an email (V2) to the District Chief Counsel shared mailbox
Post an adaptive card in Teams to District Chief Counsel requesting acknowledgment
Update item: 'District Chief Counsel notified' = utcNow()
On card response, update item: 'District Chief Counsel acknowledged' = response time

starter_flows.trigger: SharePoint – When an item is created in 'Institutional Disclosure Checklist'
actions: Get item (case number, modality, reason not in person, designated note author)
Create a Planner task for the note author: 'Enter CPRS Institutional Disclosure of Adverse Event note', including the remote-disclosure reason if the modality is not in person
Do until 'CPRS note entered' = Yes: delay (configurable interval), then send a Teams reminder to the note author

starter_flows.trigger: Power Apps (V2) – Risk Manager submits the Adverse Event Intake form
actions: Create item in 'Adverse Event Escalations' with case number, discovery date/time, reporter, harm summary, and single vs multiple patients
Send email (V2) and Teams message at the same time to the Associate Director for Patient Care Services, the Chief of Staff, and the facility Director
Post an adaptive card to the facility Director to classify the event
Update item: Disclosure path from the Director's response (systems issue → starts the A6 Issue Brief flow; single-patient → starts A5)
starter_flows.approval_step: Facility Director responds to the adaptive card choosing 'Systems issue affecting multiple patients' or 'Single-patient event that may require institutional disclosure' (decision D4)
